_purpose: Column and category mapping for scripts/import_eicv7.py. Fill this from the EICV7 codebook shipped with the extract, then run the importer. Nothing here is pre-filled with guessed EICV7 variable names: a wrong guess would import the wrong column silently, which is worse than an explicit error.

_how_to_fill.columns: Map each source variable name to a contract column name. Keys are the names as they appear in your extract; values are from _contract_columns. A key that is not in the extract is an error.
_how_to_fill.value_maps: For every categorical contract column, map each source code or label to a value from _vocabularies. A source value with no mapping is an error rather than a default.
_how_to_fill.targets: poor and extreme_poor do not need mapping unless you pass --keep-targets: by default they are recomputed from consumption_ae against the published poverty lines.

_notes: urban, modern_floor, electricity, corrugated_roof, improved_sanitation, owns_*, health_insurance, has_momo, has_savings and shock_experienced must arrive as 0/1. Recode yes/no codes through value_maps if the extract uses strings.

consumption_ae is annual consumption per adult equivalent in RWF at January 2024 prices. If the extract is in a different price base or a monthly figure, deflate it in the pipeline before importing - the importer rejects implausible scales rather than rescaling them.
district values must be the 30 district names used in data/processed/districts.json.
If the extract carries weight, stratum and psu, map them. Their presence is what allows design-based intervals instead of resampling intervals.
